concedes: My round-2 refutation (C5's tie-break by 'earliest in turn order' is ambiguous because Aeon Engine can reverse the turn order, so two readings pick different choosers) is answered: the revised C5 drops turn order entirely and has the winner of that game pick which of the tied first losers chooses. I re-simulated the revised rule. (1) Free-for-all, A wins, B and C lose in one state-based-action check: the tie-break names a unique decider, the winner, and the chooser is always one of the tied players, who are losers, so the winner can never be the chooser (the round-1 counterexample against the 'previous chooser' fallback is gone). (2) B loses first alone, then C: no tie, B chooses, and no turn order or reversal matters. (3) Four-player pod where B and C lose together, then D, then A wins: the earliest losing moment is the B/C tie, so A picks between B and C; the mixed case is covered. (4) If the remaining players all lose together the game is a draw under 104.4a and goes to 103.1's draw sentence, which C6 leaves untouched, so the winner-based tie-break never meets a drawn game. (5) The winner is well defined in free-for-all (806.1: players compete as individuals, so 104.2c's early-loser-wins exception cannot arise). What remains is a policy objection that the winner influences who chooses, which no quoted rule forbids: 103.1 fixes only that the chooser is a loser, and the stipulation keeps that. A tie-branch fact is also not stated separately from F3, and a first loser who has left the match is unspecified, but those are drafting gaps and gaps shared with 103.1, not contradictions with an official source. I find no step where the case's sequence differs from real game flow.

concede_evidence.excerpt: the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn
If all the players remaining in a game lose simultaneously, the game is a draw.
In Free-for-All multiplayer games, a group of players compete as individuals against each other.
This happens immediately and overrides all effects that would preclude that player from winning the game.
